## Purpose

This SOP describes the complete workflow for determining
$\delta^{13}$C, $\delta^{15}$N, and elemental concentrations (%C, %N)
in soil and sediment samples by combustion on the Thermo Scientific
Flash IRMS Elemental Analyzer (EA) coupled to the Delta V IRMS through
the ConFlo IV interface [@werner2001]. It covers sample preparation,
sequence design, the analytical run, and post-analysis data correction
including blank correction, linearity correction, scale normalization,
and drift correction [@paul2007; @coplen2011].

For general instrument operation, startup/shutdown, gas checks, tuning,
and pre-analysis tests, see
[SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Soil, sediment, and plant tissue samples analyzed for
  $\delta^{13}$C, $\delta^{15}$N, %C, and %N by combustion EA-IRMS in
  NC (dual reactor) mode.
- **Does not apply to:** Sulfur isotope analysis (NCS mode; requires
  dedicated reactor and Sulfinert column), GasBench applications
  (see [SOP-L415](SOP-L415-carbonate-gasbench-irms.qmd)), TC/EA
  applications ($\delta^{2}$H, $\delta^{18}$O), or liquid samples.
- **Location:** Sample preparation in SGM Rm 133; analysis in the
  Oxtoby Isotope Lab, SGM Rm 135.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                           |
|:------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve methods, oversee data quality                    |
| Lab Manager       | Prepare/verify Isodat methods; maintain reactors         |
| Certified User    | All steps from sample prep through data reduction        |
| Student Researcher| May perform sample prep and data reduction under supervision |


## Definitions

- **Blank correction:** Subtraction of the isotopic and elemental
  contribution of an empty tin capsule from each sample signal;
  necessary because capsule tin contributes a small amount of C and N
  [@paul2007].
- **$\delta^{13}$C:** Stable carbon isotope ratio expressed in per mil
  (‰) relative to Vienna Pee Dee Belemnite (VPDB): $\delta^{13}C =
  \left(\tfrac{R_\text{sample}}{R_\text{standard}} - 1\right)\times
  1000$ where $R = {}^{13}C/{}^{12}C$ [@coplen2011].
- **$\delta^{15}$N:** Stable nitrogen isotope ratio expressed in per
  mil (‰) relative to atmospheric N~2~ (AIR): $\delta^{15}N =
  \left(\tfrac{R_\text{sample}}{R_\text{standard}} - 1\right)\times
  1000$ where $R = {}^{15}N/{}^{14}N$ [@coplen2011].
- **Drift correction:** Adjustment for systematic temporal change in
  measured $\delta$ values during a sequence, estimated from
  bracketing reference materials [@paul2007].
- **Flash EA:** The Thermo Scientific Flash IRMS Elemental Analyzer
  peripheral; combusts samples at 1020 °C in an O~2~ pulse and
  separates N~2~ and CO~2~ chromatographically before delivery to the
  IRMS via the ConFlo IV.
- **Isodat:** ThermoFisher software used to design analytical
  sequences, control the instrument, and export raw isotope data.
- **Linearity correction:** Adjustment applied to account for the
  dependence of measured $\delta$ values on peak signal amplitude.
- **Reference material (RM):** A substance with a certified or
  consensus $\delta$ value used to anchor measured values to the VPDB
  or AIR scale [@werner2001].
- **Scale normalization:** Two-point (or multi-point) correction that
  maps measured $\delta$ values to the international isotope-ratio
  scale using certified RMs spanning the expected sample range
  [@paul2007].
- **Tin capsule:** 5 x 9 mm pressed-tin container used to encapsulate
  solid samples; tin ignites in the O~2~ pulse, raising combustion
  temperature briefly to ensure complete combustion.


## Safety and Hazards

See [SOP-L208, Section 4](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd) for the
full hazard list.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Application-Specific Hazards

- **Tin capsule handling:** Tweezers must be clean and dry; oils from
  fingers contaminate capsules and introduce C/N blanks.
- **Compressed gases:** He carrier and O~2~ combustion gas; see
  SOP-L208 for gas handling requirements.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (sample prep and capsule loading)

### Required Training

- [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
- [SOP-L208 IRMS General Instrument Use](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd)
  (must be a certified IRMS User before independent operation)

## Estimated Time

| Task                          | Time                          |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|
| Sample weighing (per capsule) | 3--5 min                      |
| Sequence setup in Isodat      | 20--30 min                    |
| Analytical run (per sample)   | ~7 min (N~2~ + CO~2~ in series) |
| Data reduction (R script)     | 30--60 min                    |


## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1. Dry samples at 60 °C to constant mass per
   [SOP-L105](SOP-L105-drying-ovens.qmd).
2. Grind and homogenize to <150 µm per
   [SOP-L116](SOP-L116-sample-grinding-homogenization.qmd).
3. For carbonate removal (inorganic C), acidify with 1 M HCl, re-dry,
   and record the treatment in the lab notebook before proceeding.
4. Clean the micro-balance pan and zero the balance.
5. Using clean tweezers, place a tin capsule on the balance. Tare.
6. Weigh 10--30 mg of ground sample into the capsule (adjust to keep
   the N~2~ and CO~2~ peaks within the instrument's linear range).
7. Fold and crimp the capsule tightly, removing all air.
8. Record the capsule mass in the lab notebook and in the sequence
   spreadsheet.

### Sequence Design

1. Open Isodat Sequence Editor and load the NC dual-reactor method.
2. Build the sequence in this order:
   - 3--5 conditioning samples (similar matrix to unknowns)
   - 1 blank capsule
   - Bracketing RMs (at least 2 certified materials, e.g., USGS40 +
     USGS41a for $\delta^{13}$C; IAEA-N1 + IAEA-N2 for $\delta^{15}$N)
   - Unknowns, with 1 RM per 10 samples
   - Check standard at end
   - 1 blank capsule at end
3. Save the sequence file as `YYYYMMDD_Project_SeqID_User.seq`.

### Analytical Run

1. Complete the pre-analysis checklist in SOP-L208.
2. Load the capsule plate into the Flash EA autosampler carousel.
3. Press **Start** in Isodat.
4. Monitor the first 5 injections for expected peak shape and
   amplitude.

### Post-Analysis Data Correction

Apply corrections in this order using the R script in the project
repository:

```{r}
#| label: data-correction-outline
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Import raw Isodat export (.csv)
raw <- read_csv("data/raw/YYYYMMDD_Project_SeqID_User_raw.csv")

# 2. Blank correction
#    Subtract mean blank d13C and blank area from each sample

# 3. Linearity correction
#    Regress RM d-values on peak amplitude; apply slope correction

# 4. Scale normalization (two-point)
#    Use two certified RMs to anchor measured values to VPDB / AIR

# 5. Drift correction
#    Regress RM residuals on run order; apply time-based correction

# 6. QC evaluation
#    Check RM recoveries; flag samples outside ±0.3 permil
```


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Reference material $\delta^{13}$C and $\delta^{15}$N must recover
  within ±0.2‰ of certified values after all corrections.
- Blank capsules must produce peak areas below 0.5 Vs (N~2~) and
  1 Vs (CO~2~).
- Replicate analyses of a check standard (n >= 3) must show SD
  <= 0.15‰.
- Flag and investigate any sequence where >20% of RMs fall outside
  acceptance criteria before reporting results.


## Data Management

1. Export raw data from Isodat immediately after the run as `.csv`.
2. Save under `data/raw/YYYYMMDD_Project_SeqID_User_raw.csv` in the
   project repository.
3. Commit raw data and the R correction script per
   [SOP-L801](SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd).
4. Store all corrected data in `data/processed/`.

## Training Record

Before performing soil CN analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd) in
   full
2. Be a certified IRMS User (SOP-L208, Training Record)
3. Demonstrate capsule preparation under supervision (5 capsules,
   masses within ±0.05 mg of target)
4. Perform a supervised analytical run with acceptable QC results
5. Complete at least one supervised data reduction session
6. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
